key: Read the TSH first: a failing gland releases the brake on the pituitary, so TSH rises in primary disease and is low or inappropriately normal in central disease.
items: A failing gland releases pituitary feedback, so TSH climbs as free T4 falls.
Autoimmune destruction of follicles is the commonest cause of primary hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas.
Radioiodine destroys the gland itself, so the pituitary responds with a high TSH.
Without iodine the gland cannot make hormone, TSH rises and drives the goiter.
Lithium blocks hormone release from the gland, a thyroid-level defect with a high TSH.
These antibodies mark autoimmune thyroid disease, which injures the gland itself.
The gland is idle because its stimulus is missing, the signature of central disease.
Postpartum pituitary infarction removes thyrotrophs along with the other anterior pituitary cells.
Surgery can remove or damage thyrotrophs, leaving a healthy gland without TSH.
Stalk compression cuts TRH delivery to the pituitary, a hypothalamic-pituitary cause.
Other anterior pituitary hormones also low
Several failing axes at once point to the pituitary, not to the thyroid alone.
Without TRH the thyrotrophs are not driven, so TSH and free T4 both fall.
